comment: The name is a postpositional phrase, so the clause has S and X, not A and P.

translation: The child has broken the mirror.
The letter will be written by Kitso.
comment: The index is printed cl1; (6c) prints cl11 for the same form.

translation: The letter will be written by Sékou.
comment: No verbal marking: a flexivalency alternation the book describes in the same terms as the Tswana passive (1), with the agent optionally an oblique.

translation: The letter was written by Sékou.
comment: The completive positive is marked differently in transitive and intransitive constructions independently of any valency alternation; the suffix is not voice marking.
Auxiliary selection registers the presence of an ergative slot, not the alternation: P-ambitransitivity, not equipollent voice marking.

translation: We will seek work for your friend.
comment: Neither stem is derived from the other: equipollent marking, the construction without the beneficiary taken as initial by semantic markedness.

translation: I'll write the letter to/for Kitso.
The letter will be written by me.
They will make me write the letter.
comment: The initial A is coded as P: still a core term, so not denucleativized.

translation: The cook flavors the porridge with meat.
Meat gives flavor to the porridge.
comment: The same suffix as in P-applicativization; the instrument takes over the A role and the initial A cannot be expressed, understood as non-specific.

translation: The letter will be written by Kitso.
comment: The index is printed cl1; (6c) prints cl11 for the same form.
P keeps its coding; the A/S index slot holds an expletive.
Literally 'There will be cried'.

primaryText: Ali ŋa-ndi tasu di Musa se.
translation: Ali had Moussa eat the rice.
comment: The causee takes the dative postposition.
The preverb also bounds the event; in (17) it changes aktionsart alone.

primaryText: Í yé í lá dèndìkôo nó-ndì lè.

translation: Gáleto looked at himself (in the mirror) before going out.
comment: The two participant roles are cumulated by the single S term.

translation: I had the anchor sunk (me negatively affected).
(Be careful,) the child might fall down.
(Be careful,) the child might fall into the well.
comment: The destination cannot be expressed with the underived verb.

translation: I'll write the letter to Mpho.
Kitso will make me write the letter.
Kitso will make someone write a letter to Mpho.
comment: The initial A is not mentioned but could be coded as a third P.

translation: A letter will be written to Mpho.
comment: Literally 'Mpho will be written.to a letter': the applied P takes A coding and the construction stays transitive.

translation: Someone will make me write a letter.
comment: Literally 'I will be made to write a letter': the initial A regains A coding.

translation: Someone will make someone else write a letter to Mpho.
comment: Literally 'Mpho will be made written.to a letter'.

translation: I am making you eat the meat.
I am making you eat (unspecified things).
comment: Antipassivization of a double-P construction: the derived construction stays transitive.

translation: They are making you eat the meat.
comment: Literally 'You are made to eat the meat'; 'they' is non-specific. UNVERIFIED: the meat's P status follows the analysis of Tswana (38f); the verb shows no P index.

translation: They are making you eat (unspecified things).

comment: Agent voice, derived by prefixing a nasal to the patient-voice form.
Patient voice: the pivot is the preverbal phrase.

primaryText: B<um>ili ang lalake ng isda sa tindahan.
translation: The man bought fish at the store.
comment: Agent voice.

primaryText: B<in>ili-Ø ng lalake ang isda sa tindahan.
translation: The man bought fish at the store.
comment: Patient voice; the system has no basic voice, and the agent voice is taken as initial for the comparison only.

primaryText: B<in>ilh-an ng lalake ng isda ang tindahan.
translation: The man bought fish at the store.
comment: Locative voice.

primaryText: I-b<in>ili ng lalake ng isda ang bata.
translation: The man bought fish for the child.
comment: Conveyance voice.

primaryText: Ip<in>am-bili ng lalake ng isda ang pera.
translation: The man bought fish with the money.
comment: Instrumental voice.

primaryText: I meme meli nasi sig anak-e ento.
translation: Mother bought rice from that person.

primaryText: I meme meli-in anak-e ento nasi.
translation: Mother bought rice from that person.
I made him/her kiss his/her little brother/sister.
comment: The initial P is denucleativized: valency is unchanged although a participant is nucleativized.
The prefix is glossed as an agent voice or a transitivity marker.
The noun phrase after the verb is unflagged; di- is glossed as a patient voice.

translation: Tomo has been met by them.
comment: The noun phrase after the verb is flagged by oleh; di- is glossed as a passive. The source is given as Sneddon 1996: 255, 257.

translation: The woman made the child cry.

comment: The same suffix as the causative of (2): 'The woman brought the food' implies 'The woman came'. Chapter 12 counts this use as causativization in the broad sense, portative derivation being a variety of it.
Inanimate objects can be brought but cannot come: the food is not the initial S.
